reason: B is slightly better because it more precisely links the solid-state intervention to suppression of liquid-phase hot cracking and proposes a focused service-representative comparison with measurable fatigue, crack-growth, residual-stress, and microstructural outcomes. Both remain underspecified for a high-temperature HEA—especially alloy composition, repair geometry, temperature/stress limits, and possible creep or grain-growth effects—and provide no supporting prior evidence.
